q: If a body is dropped from a height near the earth's surface, the body will fall with a ____.
e: Near the Earth's surface, freely falling objects experience a nearly constant downward acceleration.

q: If the ____ is neglected, the fall of the body is defined as free fall.
e: Free fall assumes that gravity is the only force acting on the object.

q: Equation of motion under ____ described in chapter 2 can be used in the free fall.
e: The standard kinematic equations apply to free fall because the acceleration due to gravity is constant.

q: In these equations we will use the symbol ____ for displacement s and g for acceleration a.
e: In free fall problems, vertical displacement is typically represented by the variable h (height).

q: Hence, the equations become $v = v_0 + gt$ and ____
e: This is the third kinematic equation adapted for free fall, relating velocity, initial velocity, acceleration, and displacement.

q: Note that the acceleration due to gravity g is directed ____ (towards the centre of the earth).
e: Gravity always pulls objects toward the center of the Earth.

q: Since acceleration g is always directed downwards its value will be ____ (i.e. $g = -9.8 \text{ ms}^{-2}$).
e: In a coordinate system where upward is positive, the downward acceleration of gravity is assigned a negative value.
